title: Flavoured tobacco ban and further tobacco tax increases
asked: Mr Cai Yinzhou asked whether the Ministry of Health will consider a total ban on flavoured tobacco to curb youth appeal, and whether further tobacco tax increases are being considered to discourage smoking.
answered_by: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
response: The Ministry of Health reviews tobacco control policies regularly to keep smoking prevalence low, and does not rule out a future ban on flavoured tobacco products or further tobacco tax increases. In supplementary answers, Ms Rahayu Mahzam said international evidence shows flavoured tobacco increases smoking initiation among youths, and that menthol cigarettes take up almost half of Singapore's cigarette market. She said the ministry is reviewing whether to introduce a ban on flavoured tobacco products.

key_points.point: The Ministry of Health reviews tobacco control policies regularly to keep smoking prevalence as low as possible.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: the Ministry of Health reviews our tobacco control policies regularly with the aim of keeping smoking prevalence as low as possible

key_points.point: The Ministry does not rule out a future ban on flavoured tobacco products and further tobacco tax increases.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: We do not rule out introducing a ban on flavoured tobacco products in the future and implementing further tobacco tax increases.

key_points.point: International evidence shows flavoured tobacco products increase smoking initiation, particularly among youths.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: there is a large body of international evidence showing that flavoured tobacco products increase smoking initiation, particularly amongst youths

key_points.point: Flavours such as menthol or fruit mask the harsh tobacco flavour and increase appeal to youths.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: the flavours, like menthol or fruit, are used to mask the harsh tobacco flavour and this actually increases its appeal to the youths

key_points.point: Menthol cigarettes take up almost half of Singapore's cigarette market.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: it is still fairly accurate that menthol cigarettes take up almost half of Singapore's cigarette market

key_points.point: The Ministry is reviewing whether to introduce a ban on flavoured tobacco products.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: we are reviewing as to whether or not we will introduce a ban on the flavoured tobacco products

left_open: Whether there is a correlation between the popularity of vapes and flavoured cigarettes among youths.
Whether flavoured cigarettes in Singapore are more addictive.
Plans to reduce the proportion of flavoured cigarettes sold, separate from a ban.
supplementary: Supplementary questions focused on evidence linking flavoured tobacco and vaping to youth appeal, addictiveness, market share, and plans to ban or reduce flavoured cigarettes.
